purpose: Consolidated work tracker for the Luzon delivery phase. This is not a species checklist, complete waterbody inventory, release manifest, or claim of biological absence.

limitations: The national registry supplies the pinned region, province, and separately represented independent-city baseline; its lower-level locality rows are out of scope. CALABARZON's working municipality/city name-code denominator is separately recorded in national/reviews/calabarzon-administrative-denominator-reconciliation-20261117.json; it contains no boundary geometry.
MIMAROPA is included in the Luzon delivery phase by project convention; administrative membership, island group, drainage basin, and marine study area remain separate relationships.

baselineReviewedDefinition: Use the completion gates in docs/PHILIPPINES_SPECIES_EXPANSION_PLAN.md section 3. A region is baseline-reviewed only after its complete administrative and source-derived waterbody scope is reconciled, source searches and candidate decisions are accounted for, evidence and reuse checks pass, every waterbody has an explicit coverage result, and counts reconcile.

completionGates.requirement: Account for all current provinces, applicable NCR units, independent cities, and needed lower-level locality crosswalks in the pinned administrative snapshot.
Reconcile source-derived marine, brackish, and inland waters, including rivers, tributaries, streams, natural lakes, reservoirs, wetlands, ponds, and islands where applicable.
Process each agreed source/search or record the access, rights, or evidence gap with attempted alternatives and a follow-up owner.
Give each snapshot candidate an evidence-backed admit, exclude, or hold decision. A hold is triage, not coverage.
Validate taxon identity, locality, date, provenance, item and dataset reuse terms, and citation before public projection.
Show a coverage result per inventoried waterbody; no usable record is a visible gap, never a species-absence claim.
Reconcile raw, normalized, mirrored, admitted, excluded, and held counts and list remaining gaps in each regional manifest.

regions.name: Region IV-A (CALABARZON)

appFacingResearchProjection.scope: Attributed, historical Palico-Lian survey-table assertions with unknown observation date; not a current checklist, abundance estimate, or complete regional baseline.

openWork: Reconcile the selected 164 waterbody leads and new source-derived additions against the 120-municipality/22-city locality denominator, including islands, shared waters, and freshwater, brackish, and marine lanes; this locality denominator is not a waterbody inventory.
Keep source-specific survey assertions distinct from the scope file's waterbody/public-admission counters when reconciling CALABARZON counts.

Keep Manila Bay shared with NCR and Central Luzon under one canonical waterbody identity. The 19 November National Museum crosswalk matched all 524 OBIS rows to GBIF occurrence IDs and four of seven Cavite administrative-text candidates; it adds no capture-site or Cavite-water assignment. Reconcile other sources and localities separately; see national/reviews/manila-bay-national-museum-gbif-obis-crosswalk-20261119.json.
Keep the three historical CAS Santa Cruz River records held from public projection and redistributed packages until the Academy clarifies its no-redistribution terms versus GBIF CC0 metadata.
Keep the Laguna Lakeshore Road Network EIS as a West Bay retrieval lead; its mixed 2014/2020 fish summaries lack a verified adult-fish site/date/voucher crosswalk and item-specific reuse approval.
Use independently reusable, site-resolved sources for other CALABARZON inland waters while Taal CAS redistribution terms and Dryad file access remain unresolved.
Reconcile the wetlands denominator, unnamed river/wetland counts, and modeled stream identities before claiming complete coverage.

After eight 19 November CALABARZON source-backed locality batches, the selected 164-lead scope has 80 city/municipality-linked leads, 80 province-only leads, and 4 without any locality code; represented CALABARZON coverage is 15/22 city codes and 49/120 municipality codes. BMB locality contexts include six San Pablo lakes, Yellow/Tadlac/Caliraya, three Laguna cities, three Rizal municipalities, and the separately reviewed NCR localities around one shared Laguna de Bay identity, Tanza for the Tres Cruzes candidate, Rodriguez for Wawa Dam, Cavinti for the NPC-reported Lumot Lake event locality, and the 14-LGU Taal Lake planning cluster; a working Mojicap/Mohicap alias for the San Pablo City lead is supported by LLDA lists. Retain the Tres Cruzes class/identity hold, Wawa boundaries/access limitations, Lumot reservoir extent/identity caveat, and distinguish the Taal planning cluster and all source-described localities from lake geometry. Keep scopeFrozen=false.

The 17 November exact GBIF name/alias screen returned two 1941 CAS preserved-specimen candidates for waterBody=Bay River; both remain held because locality is “3 km from Laguna de Bay” with 1,743 m uncertainty. Thirteen other exact-field searches returned zero and do not establish absence.

The cross-region 2022 PAREX EIS labels station FWE 6 as Taytay, Rizal. Keep that one-day fish-survey station separate from Laguna de Bay fish evidence and hold its locality-to-waterbody identity until independently crosswalked.

regions.name: National Capital Region (NCR)
openWork: The 17-unit NCR administrative denominator matches PSA's rendered 16-city and one-municipality tables, and PSA's revision notices support its continuity through Q3 2026; the linked workbook itself remains unparsed. The historical 18-item checkpoint is a mixed set of waterway, shared-water, reservoir, watershed, wetland-park, and habitat contexts, not 18 validated waterbodies. The 2025 DENR-NCR Gawad Taga-Ilog review crosswalks 12 selected nominations to 12 reported city/municipality codes. Follow-ups corroborate the BMB Jamboree Lake name/locality and identify a BMB NAPWC pond alias candidate plus a named OSM polygon. The polygon is community mapped; the official shoreline, BMB-to-OSM crosswalk, and conflicting 3.39 ha versus approximate 4.0 ha area descriptions remain unresolved. No current access or fish claim is established. Continue broader freshwater, brackish, marine, and habitat source searches.

Extend the source-named inventory and bounded occurrence screens across freshwater, brackish, and marine contexts without treating selected program nominations or candidate hits as a complete inventory or validated capture sites.

Keep Pasig-Marikina reaches, tidal/brackish waters, Manila Bay, and Laguna de Bay connections distinct. The 19 November crosswalk found the 65 National Museum rows from the NCR administrative query among the GBIF bounding-box records and none in the 524-row OBIS result; this is feed/query coverage, not a Manila Bay or NCR-water assignment. Reconcile other shared-bay sources with L1 and L3; see national/reviews/manila-bay-national-museum-gbif-obis-crosswalk-20261119.json.

The DENR-NCR report remains a system-scope and narrative lead without fish-by-site rows; the Marikina preprint remains an eight-taxon research crosswalk. La Mesa Reservoir has five historical host-fish candidates from a 1989-1990 parasite study (234 examined across taxa), not an abundance estimate; hold its Therapon date conflict and Arius/Netuma identity concern. Lopez (1992) is identified through a 2001 secondary citation, but the original proceedings and its methods, dates, denominators, and vouchers remain unverified. Continue freshwater, brackish, and marine source searches and reconcile all candidates against the incomplete waterbody scope.

The 2015 BMB guidebook and 2016 bulletin remain vernacular historical fish leads without traceable fish-survey methods. Five exact-text CoL XR searches returned zero. A bounded GBIF spatial search found one iNaturalist Channa striata observation inside the community-mapped OSM lagoon ring, but its 8 m uncertainty exceeds the approximately 7 m point-to-edge distance; GBIF also flags TAXON_ID_NOT_FOUND and the record has no waterBody/locality. Keep it unassigned and research-only. A secondary blog lists binomials without survey provenance; a peer-reviewed NAPWC microcrustacean study is not fish evidence. Seek a directly verifiable fish survey and review current protected-area access separately.

The 2022 PAREX Revised EIS adds a one-day, six-station fish-survey lead along the Pasig corridor, with FWE 6 labeled Taytay, Rizal. Its 14-species narrative conflicts with the 13-binomial station matrix, and Table 2-20 differs from Table 2-19. A 19 November 2026 locality crosswalk found an OSM reverse-geocoder road label in Pasig while the official MRT4 EIS lists several Taytay waterway names without linking any to the PAREX point; the station waterbody remains unresolved. Keep all names and coordinates research-only pending table reconciliation, voucher evidence, a source-matched locality link, and item-specific reuse review.

The 2019 Makati Public Rail EIS states that fish sampling at its five Pasig freshwater-ecology stations was unsuccessful; those coordinates are for plankton/benthos context, not fish occurrences. Its separate eight-name reported-fish table mixes one informal observation, two secondary citations, washout context, and unsourced rows. Keep all names research-only and continue NCR freshwater/brackish/marine source searches.

The cited Orozco & Zafaralla (2012) chapter is explicitly about Estero de San Miguel and Estero de Quiapo; its abstract reports Rasbora maculata and Anabas testudineus among four fish taxa, without species-to-station assignments. A related 2008 DLSU article describes the same two esteros and four taxa, but its full text is unavailable. Do not transfer either estero finding to Pasig River or double-count the apparent research lineage.

regions.name: Region III (Central Luzon)
openWork: The BMB 2014 Atlas count crosswalk matches the RDP's 168 breakdown at category/count level (153 river systems; 11 lakes, three reservoirs and one swamp), but source lineage, the RDP's separate 202-river statement, all 153 named river systems, current identity and geometry remain unresolved; do not treat this as a verified inventory.

The 70-query CoL XR screen returned one Angat River locality row and 69 bounded zeroes. Follow-up linked it to BPC001-13/ANAd1, source-reported as Arius dispar, while the GBIF Backbone maps the BIN to Netuma thalassina; the BOLD BIN export does not resolve that specimen. A local FAO/HydroRIVERS screen places the source coordinate 0.7 km from an unnamed modeled reach; it is inside a simplified 2020 Bulacan polygon and shares the modeled MAIN_RIV grouping nearest to the GeoNames Angat River point. This supports plausibility only: the GeoNames point is not a route, the reach is unnamed, the exact reach and coordinate uncertainty remain unresolved, and the source chains are not independent. Keep the candidate research-only. The 69 zeroes do not establish absence.
Complete separate evidence and coverage results for Pampanga River reaches, Angat and Pantabangan reservoirs, Candaba wetland, tributaries, coast and estuaries.

The corrected 12-query CoL XR exact-field screen for Paitan Lake and Vaca Dam Reservoir returned zero matching records; this is a bounded index gap, not evidence of fish absence. Continue source searches for dated, independently reusable records.

The refreshed 2020 Candaba source reports one representative specimen per species group deposited at PSAU, but no accession numbers, field dates, site matrix, or item-specific reuse license; keep it research-only pending independent checks.

The UPLB-provided 1988 Habito thesis abstract reports eight freshwater fish species in eight families from a June–October 1987 survey but provides no fish species names. The official UPLB record says the document is unavailable online and identifies a physical UPLB Main Library Special Collections holding, call number LG 995 1988 Z62 H33. Current access and reproduction rules are unknown; no taxa or maps were extracted. See national/reviews/central-luzon-candaba-habito-1988-thesis-access-review-20261119.json.

Santos et al. (2010) reports 844 Leiopotherapon plumbeus specimens aggregated across seven localities. Its ResearchGate author-uploaded text describes Maasin River as a Pampanga tributary in Barangay San Agustin, Candaba, and calls the population native; a Maasin-specific sample count, date, voucher, or item reuse license remains unverified. ResearchGate warns the upload may be copyrighted. Keep as a historical research lead; see national/reviews/central-luzon-candaba-2010-maasin-silver-perch-review-20261119.json and national/reviews/central-luzon-candaba-2010-maasin-rg-fulltext-followup-20261119.json.

The 2019 Bagac conference paper is now identified and its 17/5 totals match the goby synthesis. Keep it separate from the 2022 15-taxon survey and later three-river surveys until field dates, possible sample overlap, and reuse are resolved.

The 2024 Angat ASH abstract names five fish and broad gut-content categories, but has no dated fish-to-site matrix, voucher crosswalk, quantitative prey rows, or item-specific reuse license; retain as research-only and seek an author-hosted full paper or data supplement.

The 19 November National Museum crosswalk shows that the 524-row OBIS refresh mirrors the same GBIF occurrence records; do not count it as an independent L3 species batch. It does not resolve capture waters or other shared-bay sources. Keep Manila Bay shared with L1/L2 and Bataan, Zambales, and Aurora coastal scopes distinct; see national/reviews/manila-bay-national-museum-gbif-obis-crosswalk-20261119.json.

regions.name: Region I (Ilocos Region)
openWork: Build the region's waterbody manifest across Lower Agno, Abra, tributaries, Lingayen Gulf, coast and estuaries.
Keep Dantis and Lacap's five-station 2018 Agno macrofauna source research-only until its locality and table/taxonomy conflicts are resolved; the goby synthesis row is a bibliography lead only.
Keep the 2001 four-river edible-fauna paper held for unresolved taxonomy, site resolution, and reuse; search for independently reusable, dated river and coastal evidence.
Reconcile source-supported reach relationships with CAR without extending a reach-specific record across an entire basin.

regions.name: Region II (Cagayan Valley)
openWork: Continue the waterbody and fish-source sweep outside the Cagayan Riverine Zone, including Pacific-draining Isabela, Batanes islands, and separate Quirino and Nueva Vizcaya waters.
Keep barcode field labels, market-purchase labels, coordinates, and drainage crosswalks held until specimen, date, site, and reuse checks resolve.
Reconcile coastal, estuarine, river, reservoir, lake, wetland, aquaculture, and infrastructure records as separate evidence contexts.

regions.name: Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR)
openWork: Create a six-province inland waterbody inventory for rivers, headwaters, streams, lakes, reservoirs, rice terraces and wetlands; marine coverage is not applicable.
The Ibulao landing-center paper is an Ifugao/CAR source, not an Isabela occurrence dataset; resolve its downstream Magat connection only with station-level evidence.
Keep local/common-name interviews, fishery reports, and unverified taxonomy in research-only status until waterbody, specimen or study, date, and reuse context are adequate.
Resolve shared Abra and upper-Agno/Abra reach relationships with L4 and L5 from evidence, not region labels alone.

regions.name: Region V (Bicol Region)
openWork: Resolve conflicting scope and totals in the Bicol River study before considering any site-level projection.
Build separate fish evidence and coverage for Bicol River reaches, Buhi/Bato/Baao lakes, tributaries, San Miguel Bay, and the island/coastal provinces.
Keep the project inventory separate from aquaculture, seafood market, and risk-assessment sources; perform taxon-specific sensitivity review.

regions.name: MIMAROPA Region
openWork: Expand beyond Naujan Lake and Palawan with distinct, dated freshwater surveys or voucher-backed records for Marinduque, Occidental Mindoro, and Romblon.
Audit every island and province across marine, brackish, and inland lanes; mainland or Palawan-only coverage cannot stand in for the region.
Keep inaccessible or rights-unclear theses, reports, and occurrence mirrors held while pursuing other public and reusable sources.

requirements: Eight versioned regional scope manifests reviewed and their current administrative units accounted for.
Shared waters reconciled across regions without duplicating or widening source-specific locality claims.
Supported evidence integrated only after identity, geography, date, citation, and reuse checks.
Visible per-waterbody coverage results and unresolved research gaps published in the regional manifests.

nextExecution: Continue L2 NCR source discovery across all 17 administrative units and freshwater, brackish, and marine contexts. The 2025 DENR-NCR review crosswalks twelve selected waterway nominations to twelve reported city/municipality codes, while the historical 18-item checkpoint remains a mixed set of waterway, shared-water, reservoir, watershed, protected-wetland, and habitat contexts rather than a denominator. Reconcile the two held BMB source-row candidates and seek independent, reusable inventories for omitted rivers, creeks, ponds, wetlands, reservoirs, and coastal habitats. Keep monitoring stations separate from waterbody features, preserve shared-water identities, and do not freeze scope or publish species/geometry claims until the source, feature, rights, and locality gaps are resolved. PSA's public quarterly revisions support the 17-unit denominator through the 30 September 2026 snapshot; the linked workbook itself remains unparsed because its direct download returned a Cloudflare challenge.
